subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve distinct ACP session parallelism and require live launch-readiness proof before fixing this, or intentionally add a gate/serialization point for rapid ACP child launches?
rationale: Current source and tests deliberately allow different ACP sessions to run in parallel, while the report points to a backend launch-readiness race that was not reproduced on current main.

options.title: Preserve parallelism and prove launch readiness
options.body: Keep the current distinct-session concurrency contract, run a live ACPX/Claude two-spawn smoke, and fix the confirmed launch/readiness failure path if it reproduces.

options.title: Add an explicit ACP launch gate
options.body: Serialize or rate-limit ACP child launch initialization with tests and docs, accepting the compatibility and throughput tradeoff as intentional product behavior.

recommendation.title: Preserve parallelism and prove launch readiness
recommendation.body: Keep the current distinct-session concurrency contract, run a live ACPX/Claude two-spawn smoke, and fix the confirmed launch/readiness failure path if it reproduces.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-line and ACPX wrapper history makes this the best available routing owner for the live proof and launch-readiness/product boundary choice.
